original_question: Do there exist infinitesimal symmetries Q(P) of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds that are simultaneously nonlinear, proper, and nontrivial in Poisson cohomology, meaning they are not of the form [[P,X]] up to terms proportional to [[P,P]]? If no such examples exist, what mechanism forces all currently known universal Poisson cocycles, including those produced from nontrivial graph cocycles by O→r, to become ∂_P-trivial?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Conjecture 1.1, together with its paper-explicit reformulation via Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly isolates the paper’s cohomological open problem rather than the neighboring combinatorial or PDE questions. In particular, it already has the three paper-critical qualifiers: the symmetry should be nonlinear, proper (i.e. not vanishing merely because it is built from the Jacobiator), and nontrivial in Poisson cohomology; it also correctly identifies the relevant notion of triviality as being of the form [[P,X]] modulo terms proportional to [[P,P]]. The reference to universal Poisson cocycles obtained from graph cocycles by the orientation morphism is also aligned with the paper’s intended source of examples.
missing_details: The ambient category should be stated explicitly: finite-dimensional affine manifolds, with a Poisson bivector P viewed as a smooth bivector field satisfying the Jacobi identity [[P,P]]=0, where [[ , ]] is the Schouten bracket.

The question is about universal infinitesimal symmetries Q(P), meaning differential-polynomial bivector fields constructed functorially from P itself (in the paper, especially those encoded by oriented Kontsevich graphs), not arbitrary ad hoc symmetries depending on extra choices.

The paper’s symmetry condition is not just 'Q is a cocycle at one P' but a universal Poisson-cocycle condition: [[P,Q(P)]]=0 for every Poisson bivector P, equivalently via factorization through the Jacobiator as discussed around Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3.

The term 'proper' needs the paper’s exact meaning: Q(P) should not be an improper term that vanishes on all Poisson bivectors because it is universally proportional to the Jacobiator [[P,P]] (or to an operator applied to it).

The term 'nontrivial in Poisson cohomology' should be stated in the paper’s modulo-improper-terms sense: there should be no universal vector field X(P) and no universal operator diamond such that Q(P) = [[P,X(P)]] + diamond(P,[[P,P]]).

The draft should make explicit that 'nonlinear' excludes the linear dilation flow Q(P)=P and asks for degree at least 2 in P; in the graph language this is the homogeneous degree coming from the number of internal vertices.

The universal quantifier is important: the paper asks for existence of such a universal flow in the affine finite-dimensional setting, not merely for a single specially chosen Poisson manifold or a single concrete bivector.

If one keeps the graph-complex provenance in the question, it should be phrased as motivation or as the intended class of examples, not as a separate broader variant: the paper’s official target is the cohomological existence/nonexistence problem itself.
refined_question: Let N be a finite-dimensional affine manifold and let P be a Poisson bivector on N, so that [[P,P]]=0 in the Schouten bracket. Does there exist a universal infinitesimal symmetry Q(P) of the Jacobi identity—i.e. a homogeneous differential-polynomial bivector field functorially constructed from P (in particular, of the kind produced by Kontsevich’s oriented-graph calculus)—such that: (i) Q is nonlinear in P, (ii) Q is proper, meaning it is not an improper term universally proportional to the Jacobiator [[P,P]], and (iii) Q is nontrivial in Poisson cohomology modulo improper terms, meaning there do not exist a universal differential-polynomial vector field X(P) and a universal operator diamond with Q(P)= [[P,X(P)]] + diamond(P,[[P,P]])? Equivalently: is there a universal Poisson 2-cocycle that is simultaneously nonlinear, proper, and not ∂_P-exact modulo improper Jacobiator terms; or must every currently known universal flow collapse to such a trivialization?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, in the language of Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3: does there exist a universal Poisson 2-cocycle Q(P) for which one cannot solve the decomposition Q(P)= [[P,X(P)]] + diamond(P,[[P,P]]) by any universal differential-polynomial vector field X(P) and any universal operator diamond?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s 'third' open problem, namely the cohomological status of universal graph-generated Poisson flows, not the separate open problems on graph combinatorics or on the PDE/integrability behavior of special classes of Poisson structures. The closest official paper target is Conjecture 1.1, and the draft’s clause 'not of the form [[P,X]] up to terms proportional to [[P,P]]' matches the paper’s reformulation through Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3. What had to be added to make it stand alone was the ambient affine finite-dimensional setting, the universal/functorial nature of Q(P), the Schouten-bracket notation, the exact meaning of 'proper' as 'not improper/Jacobiator-built', and the fact that cohomological triviality is taken modulo such improper terms. The final wording stays narrow by keeping the question centered on existence/nonexistence of a universal nonlinear proper nontrivial cocycle, which is the paper’s official formulation, while retaining the graph-cocycle provenance only as the intended class of examples.
